 PROVIDENCE, R.I. (WJAR) — Providence Police Chief Oscar Perez fought back tears Tuesday as he talked about his three-decade career with the force. He says he will retire early next year.
 His last day will be Jan. 4.
 "I've been contemplating retirement for a while now, and the mayor and I spoke about this and I had promised him that I would stay until the end of his term," Perez said. "It's bitter sweet without a doubt, but I know everything comes to an end. As the mayor stated, my family has taken a back seat for years, and I think it's time I give back to them to make sure we enjoy our lives."
 As for what's next for Perez, he said he hasn't really thought about it and that he's ready to spend time with his family.
 NBC 10's Molly Levine reports that Providence Police Chief Oscar Perez will step away early next year. 
 In his resignation letter, Perez said the position brought him tremendous pride to serve his hometown.
 “After 32 years of service, I am leaving the position with tremendous pride and a heart full of gratitude for the city that shaped my childhood, provided my education and gave me opportunities that changed the course of my life,” Perez wrote in his letter.

 Perez's retirement comes as Mayor-elect David Morales is set to take office in January.
 "Colonel Oscar Perez has informed me that he plans to leave the department to spend time with his wife and focus on her care as she faces serious health challenges. My thoughts are with him, his wife, and his family. I respect his decision to put his family first, and I’m grateful for his decades of service to Providence," Morales said in a statement.
 DAN JAEHNIG REPORTS: Col. Oscar Perez's journey from Colombia to Providence police chief 
 Morales previously voiced support for defunding police but has since walked back that position.
 "My first responsibility as mayor will be to keep our neighbors across Providence safe. I’m committed to ensuring that our Providence Police Department has the resources, support, and strong, steady leadership our officers need to serve our communities effectively and keep our neighborhoods safe," Morales said.
 Providence Police Chief Col. Oscar Perez spoke with NBC 10. (WJAR) 
 Morales said he will start a search for a new police chief.
 "In the weeks ahead, we’ll conduct a thorough search for the next chief and keep community members informed along the way," said Morales. 
 Perez was named the city's first Latino police chief in February 2023. He started as a patrolman in 1994.
 Perez, originally from Medellin, Colombia, moved to Providence when he was 13 years old. He attended city schools.
 He earned his bachelor’s degree from Roger Williams University and his master's from Boston University. Perez also had specialized training, such as the FBI Academy, the Harvard Kennedy School of Government, and the Senior Management Institute of Policing.
 Perez's decision to retire comes amid other high-profile departures in Providence leadership roles.
 Providence Fire Chief Derek Silva announced his retirement last week, and Providence Public Schools superintendent Javier Montañez is also stepping down.
